short: South Africa has no AI law or adopted AI policy: the Cabinet-approved Draft National AI Policy of 10 April 2026 was withdrawn in its entirety on 12 June 2026. POPIA binds, including its rule on decisions based solely on automated processing.
title: South Africa AI Laws
subtitle: No AI law: a draft AI policy withdrawn, and POPIA on automated decisions
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI law or adopted AI policy. The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies published a Cabinet-approved Draft National Artificial Intelligence Policy for comment on 10 April 2026 (General Notice 3880 of 2026). On 12 June 2026 it was withdrawn in its entirety (General Notice 3978 of 2026), and Cabinet approved the withdrawal. South Africa therefore has no AI law and no adopted AI policy. The binding layer is the Protection of Personal Information Act, whose section 71 restricts decisions based solely on automated processing. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Government Gazette on gov.za and SAnews.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateStatus
Draft South Africa National Artificial Intelligence PolicyGeneral Notice 3880 of 2026, Government Gazette 54477Published 10 April 2026, after Cabinet approvalWithdrawn by General Notice 3978 of 2026, Gazette 54840, 12 June 2026
Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013Act No. 4 of 2013; Gazette 37067Assented to 19 November 2013; published 26 November 2013In force

Who regulates and enforces

  • Information Regulator: enforces POPIA, including section 71.
  • Department of Communications and Digital Technologies: owns AI policy.

Scope and reach

POPIA applies to responsible parties domiciled in South Africa, and to those not domiciled there that use automated or non-automated means in South Africa, unless the means are used only to forward information through the country (s. 3(1)(b)).

Core obligations

  • A data subject may not be subject to a decision with legal consequences or a substantial effect that is based solely on automated processing intended to profile them, except as section 71(2) allows (POPIA s. 71(1)).
  • The rest of POPIA's conditions for lawful processing.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
An offence dealt with by infringement noticeAn administrative fine of up to R10 millionPOPIA s. 109(2)(c)Information Regulator
Offences under ss. 100, 103(1), 104(2), 105(1) and 106(1), (3) and (4)A fine, imprisonment of up to 10 years, or bothPOPIA s. 107(a)Courts

What is coming next

  • A reworked AI policy; Cabinet said the policy would be revised, and no official date has been published.

Related

  • Global AI Laws: every jurisdiction compared, with the world map
  • AI Policy Ledger, the law tracker
  • AI lawsuit tracker and AI news

Sources

  • General Notice 3880 of 2026, the draft AI policy, Government Gazette
  • General Notice 3978 of 2026, withdrawal, Government Gazette
  • Cabinet approves withdrawal of AI policy, SAnews
  • Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013, gov.za

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: the 2024 National AI Policy Framework, because the department's website was under maintenance, and press reports of a revised policy timetable.
